ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. The maximum feasible transaction semantics for workflow/tool orchestration under H1-H8 is: (i) [RESOURCE_BOUNDED — fsync-scoped, relative to the declared storage platform] for all effects on media the system controls: strict-serializable, single-commit-point atomicity — a multi-object transition becomes visible through exactly one atomic switch, with durability exactly at the declared platform's write-barrier point and read-back-verified persistence, such that after a crash at ANY instant the recovered state is exactly sigma_pre or exactly sigma_post, never a hybrid; the atomicity/durability point moves with the declared platform (persistent-memory atomic units, battery-backed caches, and replication each relocate it — outside a single-node declared model they are resources, not impossibilities); (ii) [ABSOLUTE] for effects on media the system does NOT control (network calls to external tools/publishers): exactly-once is unattainable — the two-generals/atomic-commitment impossibility is model-independent; the ceiling is journaled intent/outcome with idempotency keys and compensations, with the irrevocable external act structurally excluded from the atomic section and an unknowable external outcome parked in typed UNKNOWN (H2/H3).
derivation: (i) is a storage bound relative to the declared platform: stable storage exposes bounded atomic units and reorders un-fenced writes, so multi-object atomicity must be manufactured by funneling validity through one atomic commit record behind explicit barriers. Taxonomy claim restated honestly (v1 overclaim corrected): every KNOWN correct protocol family reduces to a single atomic pointer/record switch — write-ahead logging, shadow-paging, and their copy-on-write/log-structured hybrids — and this REDUCTION is the load-bearing claim the machine-checked obligation must prove, not a folk-theorem to assert. You cannot be more atomic than one atomic switch on the declared platform, nor durable earlier than the barrier that puts the commit record on stable media; read-back verification is the ceiling of durability EVIDENCE (H8). Clause (i) is RESOURCE_BOUNDED for the same reason AX-15 is: it is scoped to the declared single-node POSIX platform whose fsync semantics define the durable point. (ii) is the genuinely ABSOLUTE half: committing atomically across parties with independent failure modes requires a coordinator round that cannot be simultaneously non-blocking and safe in the two-generals limit; since external parties grant no transactional interface, the honest ceiling is intent-journal before, outcome-journal after, idempotency keys for at-least-once retry, compensation, and typed UNKNOWN for unknowable outcomes. H6 fixes the composition: every trusted-state mutation routes through the single atomic commit of (i), making partial workflow effects in the canonical store structurally impossible.
ceiling_kind: RESOURCE_BOUNDED (clause i, fsync-scoped on the declared platform) / ABSOLUTE (clause ii, two-generals/atomic-commitment impossibility)
relativity_note: The v1 uniform ABSOLUTE label was kind-inconsistent with AX-15's RESOURCE_BOUNDED label over identical storage physics; v2 carves clause (i) as RESOURCE_BOUNDED and retains ABSOLUTE only for clause (ii).
lean_obligation: Model a POSIX-like disk as a labeled transition system with write/fsync/fsyncdir/rename where rename of a directory entry is atomic, un-fsynced writes may be reordered/dropped at a crash, and crash is enabled at every step. For commit protocol P and recovery R prove crash refinement of the atomic specification: every behavior of (P; crash*; R) recovers exactly sigma_pre or sigma_post, with sigma_post iff the commit-record rename was durably applied; recovery idempotence R(R(b)) = R(b); durability soundness: success implies every subsequent crash recovers sigma_post. REDUCTION obligation (new in v2): prove that any protocol in the WAL, shadow-paging, and CoW/log-structured hybrid families satisfying the atomicity spec factors through a single atomic switch — the taxonomy claim as theorem, not assertion. For clause (ii): prove no protocol over an unreliable channel achieves common knowledge of commit (two-generals), and that the intent/outcome journal with idempotency keys yields at-most-once observable effect on committed state under at-least-once retry.

attainment_witness_appendix.candidate_mechanism: Implement commit-accepted-transition! of STORAGE-API.sexp as a shadow-commit protocol in SBCL with sb-posix: (1) write the six items to temp files, fsync each; (2) write a commit record naming the six items with SHA-256 and the new sequence, fsync it and the directory; (3) atomic rename of the commit record IS the commit point; fsync directory; (4) recovery recomputes all six hashes, rolls forward a complete commit or removes orphans; (5) read-back verification per require-durable! (adoption-decision.lisp:99); (6) single-writer premise is the proven OS-DAC closure; (7) external tool calls move to an intent/outcome journal with idempotency keys outside the atomic section. The machine-checked Lean 4 crash-refinement proof replaces the externally-blocked Perennial/GoTxn route — proof, not tests, remains the substrate.
attainment_witness_appendix.b0_gap_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the six-item transaction is specification-only (:implementation-status :absent-by-design, :production-writer :disabled); the actual canonical writer emit-graph (write-authority.lisp:47) opens with :if-exists :supersede and no fsync or temp-rename — a crash mid-write leaves a truncated canonical artifact, the exact hybrid the ceiling forbids; durability discipline covers only governance ledgers; no external intent/outcome journal exists.
